newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIA GAS OIL/JET - AMPLE OFFERS HOLD DIESEL STEADY.
newsitem.headline: ASIA GAS OIL/JET - AMPLE OFFERS HOLD DIESEL STEADY.

text.p: Singapore's gas oil prices were unaffected by firmer crude levels as offers flooded the market amid lack of demand, traders said on Tuesday.
Several cargoes lifting end-August to early September were offered on the gas oil market, in the range of $22.80 to $23.50 per barrel.
But no buying interest emerged.
A western trader who had been buying cargoes since last week was absent in the market on Tuesday.
Traders said that he had been buying to cover a short position into Indonesia, and had accumulated enough volumes following its last purchase from a major on Monday.
Taiwan's tender to sell early September gas oil which closed on Monday would only be awarded on Wednesday, an official said.
But traders said that up to six bids were submitted into the tender, at discounts ranging between 50 to 90 cents per barrel under Singapore spot quotes, free-on-board Taiwan.
In its last gas oil sell tender, Taiwan awarded two cargoes around $20.30-20.50 fob.
Sri Lanka cancelled its buy tender for early September 1.0 percent gas oil, and jet due to high stocks.
Traders did not expected this to have a big impact on the market, since it was for 1.0 percent material and the volumes were quite small.
But it did not help the already bearish market, they said.
Jet prices fell on ample supplies.
A trade was done at $22.80 for August 27-31 between traders, after sellers had offerred continuously lower levels since last week.
But some traders still thought the level traded was above the market.
"I would assess it lower looking at fundamentals, but since there is someone willing to pay at that level, I guess that's where prices are going to land at today," said a trader.
Traders said that the buyer could be buying to cover an early September Taiwan tender that he had been awarded previously, but this could not be confirmed.
